mainExecutable.note: The app's executable holds our code, the Mono runtime and the native code of .NET for iOS, which the build links into it, and the code of the packages that the app ships, which full ahead-of-time compilation puts into it (C-0003 section 3, C-0009 section 3). tools/GenerateNotices.cs maps it to the component of every package in the app's lock file, through eng/license-map.json, including packages that do not ship: build tasks, the native assets of other platforms and assemblies that the trimmer removes. That errs on the side of a notice too many. The ahead-of-time data of the generic instances that the compiler shares between all assemblies, aot-instances.aotdata.arm64, comes from the whole app in the same way.

.NET for iOS (dotnet/macios).note: Two runtime packs: Microsoft.iOS with the bindings, and Microsoft.iOS.Runtimes with the native code for ios-arm64 that the build links into the executable. Each carries the LICENSE of dotnet/macios, the MIT license followed by the notices of the third-party code that it carries, which the notices hold once.

.NET runtime.note: The runtime pack that the app's build uses, Mono's for iOS. Its THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.TXT names parts under Apache-2.0 without the license's terms, so the full Apache-2.0 text follows, from a pinned copy that is byte for byte the text at apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt, marked as carrying Apache-2.0 so that the notices title it by that license and do not list kubernetes/kubernetes among the sources; a notice too many is the accepted way to err, and the coverage review of M9.1 confirms which parts ship.

Avalonia.credit: BidiReorderer.cs in Avalonia.Base is a modified C# port of linear-reorder.c of fribidi/linear-reorder at commit f2f8722.

missing.text: the notice of the Stack Overflow answer https://stackoverflow.com/a/15994225, whose computation and comments PinchGestureRecognizer.cs in Avalonia.Base takes
missing.note: Stack Overflow publishes its answers under CC BY-SA, which C-0003 section 5 does not list, and no file on raw.githubusercontent.com holds the notice; the coverage review of M9.1 decides with recelilious whether and how it ships (docs/design/release-engineering.md section 10).

Avalonia.note: Avalonia's packages declare MIT and ship no license or notice file; their nuspecs record the repository commit 2d79ba55 of 12.1.4. The texts come from that commit and from the projects that its code names as sources. licence.md is Avalonia's own license as upstream wrote it. NOTICE.md holds the notices of the third-party code in Avalonia's repository, part of which is inside the shipped assemblies, such as Avalonia.Base, Avalonia.Controls and Avalonia.Skia: WPF, the Silverlight Toolkit under Ms-PL, wayland-protocols, Metsys.Bson, RichTextKit under Apache-2.0, Mono, Collections.Pooled, EllipticalArc.java, WinUI, Chromium, Flutter and Reactive Extensions; Metsys.Bson is in Avalonia.Remote.Protocol, which neither bundle holds. Lines 1 to 3 of BiDiAlgorithm.cs hold the notice of Six Labors, another holder of Apache-2.0 code in Avalonia.Base besides Ascora GmbH below, which NOTICE.md does not list. Lines 1 to 26 of SpringSolver.cs hold Apple's BSD-2-Clause notice of the WebKit code that it ports, and lines 1 to 38 of fribidi/linear-reorder's linear-reorder.c Google's notice of the reordering that BidiReorderer.cs ports; its terms ask for a notice in the documentation that the code was modified, which the credit gives. The full Apache-2.0 text comes from a pinned copy that is byte for byte the text at apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt, since RichTextKit's license.txt holds only the short notice; it is marked as carrying Apache-2.0, as in the .NET runtime's entry. LottieSharp's LICENSE at ab704fa, of 2018-09-19, is Apache-2.0 with the copyright of Ascora GmbH; ColorAnimator.cs already carried its comment on LottieSharp's color interpolation in Avalonia's commit 00167d61 of 2018-12-08, within that Apache-2.0 period, which ended when LottieSharp moved to MIT in 2022. LineBreak.cs and UnicodeTrie.cs are ported from foliojs/linebreak and foliojs/unicode-trie, and RelativePanel.cs in Avalonia.Controls from HandyControl, so their MIT licenses follow. The last text is the Unicode License V3 of unicode-org/cldr at e0748bce, with the copyright years 2004-2026 of Unicode, Inc., for the data that Avalonia.Base generates from the Unicode Character Database 17.0.0, whose files carry a copyright of 2025; the .NET runtime's notice of the Unicode data ends in 2024. It is marked as carrying Unicode-3.0, since cldr is not a source of Avalonia's code. docs/design/release-engineering.md section 4 records the scan of the shipped assemblies' source that found these notices.

Avalonia.BuildServices.note: It declares MIT and ships no license file; its nuspec records the repository commit 777f975, whose LICENSE is the text, as upstream wrote it.

HarfBuzzSharp.note: The native-asset package lists the further components of the native library in its THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (C-0003 section 6).

MicroCom.Runtime.note: It declares MIT and ships no license file.

protobuf-net.note: protobuf-net and protobuf-net.Core declare Apache-2.0 and ship neither a license file nor a NOTICE file, and the copyright of their description only points to the repository. Their nuspecs record the repository commit 3aa672e, whose Licence.txt holds protobuf-net's copyright notice and its short Apache-2.0 notice, as upstream wrote it; the repository has no NOTICE file at that commit. The full Apache-2.0 text follows from the pinned copy of the .NET runtime's entry, marked as carrying Apache-2.0.

QR code generator (Net.Codecrete.QrCodeG.note: Net.Codecrete.QrCodeGenerator declares MIT and ships no license file; its nuspec records the repository commit 6d9546e, whose LICENSE is the library's own, as upstream wrote it. The library began as a C# port of the Java version of Project Nayuki's QR Code generator library, which is MIT too, and its register row keeps Nayuki's notice beside its own (C-0003 section 6): lines 1 to 22 of that version's QrCode.java at the release v1.8.0, its leading comment, hold the notice and the license.

SkiaSharp.note: The native-asset package lists the further components of the native library in its THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (C-0003 section 6).

source.note: C-0003 section 3 and C-0009 section 6: the library's complete source at the commit of the release tag 4.0.0-Beta.2, which the package's nuspec names too. It holds the library, the definitions in the submodule Resources/Protobufs and in Resources/SteamLanguage that its generated code comes from, the generators ProtobufGen and SteamLanguageParser, the files that build and pack it (the root's build files, its strong-name key, the two files of Resources/Misc that the package takes) and the upstream's workflows that build, pack and regenerate it. NetHook2, whose headers come from the Steamworks SDK that C-0003 section 5 forbids, NetHookAnalyzer2, ProtobufDumper, Resources/Structs, the other files of Resources/Misc, the samples, the tests and the solution files stay out. Moving the pin is a reviewed change of its own.

SteamKit2.note: The package's license.txt is a short LGPL notice and not the LGPL-2.1 text, so the full text follows from external/Paneport-wine/COPYING.LIB, at the commit that this repository records, which the ios job checks out before the notices step. Its 3rd party.txt names protobuf-net, whose texts are in that component's entry. The part of the LZMA SDK that its register row names is in the public domain and needs no text. SteamKit2 is the one LGPL component that full ahead-of-time compilation puts into the executable (C-0003 section 3).

ZstdSharp (ZstdSharp.Port).note: ZstdSharp.Port declares MIT and ships no license file; its nuspec records the repository commit 2cd0c01, whose LICENSE is the port's MIT license with the porter's copyright, as upstream wrote it. The port is based on Zstandard v1.5.7, which is BSD-3-Clause or GPL-2.0-only; the ported code is used under BSD-3-Clause, and its register row keeps Zstandard's notice beside the port's (C-0003 section 6): the LICENSE of facebook/zstd at the release v1.5.7.
